claim: To post a job for Penn State engineering students, you should use **Nittany Lion Careers**, which is the university's free job posting platform for internship, co-op, and full-time opportunities across all majors and campuses.

To create an account, go to the Nittany Lion Careers login page, select **Employers**, and choose either **Sign Up** (to create your profile) or **Sign Up and Post Job** (if you have positions ready to post).
To be eligible, your organization must have a functioning organizational website, a verifiable business address, and a recruiter email address that matches your organization's domain.
After you complete and submit the registration form, career staff will review and approve your account and postings before students can view them, usually within one business day.
Monday through Friday).

The hiring guidelines for recruiting Penn State engineering students are adapted from the National Association for Colleges and Employers (NACE) Principles for Professional Conduct for Career Services & Employment Professionals.

Employers must follow Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and affirmative action principles, considering students without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.

Penn State may flag selection practices that appear discriminatory, help employers reach a broader and more inclusive student audience, and respond to complaints of EEO noncompliance by working with employers to resolve them or referring them to the appropriate campus department or agency.
The guidelines also include specific testing policies for employers who use assessments in their hiring process.
These guidelines are available on the "Hiring Best Practices & Recruiting Guidelines" page at career.engr.psu.edu/employers/guidelines.aspx.
For recruiting questions in the College of Engineering, contact Autumn Eyer, Recruiting Manager/Nittany.
You can post internship, co-op, and entry-level jobs in Nittany Lion Careers.
If you have questions about posting jobs, contact the office.
The College of Engineering has strong relationships with industry and government employers, and hundreds of technical employers recruit at Penn State each year.

Department of Homeland Security’s Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) now requires that CPT only be approved if an off-campus internship is required for all students in the degree program and the degree cannot be completed without it.
Since students in the College of Engineering are not required to complete internships as a condition of graduation, they are no longer eligible for CPT.

However, international students with approved summer 2026 CPT who are currently finishing up their summer internships may do so, and students who had CPT approved prior to August 12 for a fall 2026 internship may still complete their internship.

Students may still complete on-campus research positions, on-campus non-professional positions (e.g., dining commons), and short-term work experiences outside of the U.S., as these options do not require CPT.

The Recruiting Partners Program is a partnership between the College of Engineering and participating employers that provides strategic assistance with recruiting, enhanced access to target populations, and increased opportunities for visibility in the College of Engineering.
The program costs $10,000 per fiscal year (July 1–June 30).

Benefits include personalized assistance with developing a strategic recruiting, branding, and engagement plan, priority access to interview space and recruiting event scheduling, and one complimentary recruiting day or similar event per academic year ($1,000 value).
The program also offers assistance in executing up to two targeted student recruiting events per academic year, such as information sessions, mock interview sessions, or résumé review sessions.
Additionally, partners receive exclusive invitations to provide professional development presentations and activities for engineering students and facilitated access to student organizations.

The Engineering/EECS Affiliates Program is a collaborative program between Engineering Career Resources & Employer Relations and the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) intended to help maximize connections between students in EECS majors and employers seeking to hire them.
It costs $15,000 per fiscal year (July 1–June 30).

Program benefits include personalized assistance with developing a strategic recruiting, branding, and engagement plan with both Engineering Career Resources & Employer Relations and the School of EECS.

Additional benefits include sponsor placement at the annual School of EECS Day ($2,000 value) with front-row placement at the networking reception, company logo featured on the event website and searchable database, up to ten representatives at the event, and priority access to interview space and recruiting event scheduling.

Your company can collaborate with Penn State Engineering faculty through research partnerships, research sponsorship, or by joining the Partner Advisory Board with the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
The department already collaborates with industry partners such as Lockheed Martin, Pratt & Whitney, and Solar Turbines through direct funding or joint research.
You can also engage with the Center for e-Design, a National Science Foundation Industry/University Cooperative Research Center that combines industry needs with academic resources.
To initiate a research partnership, contact the College of Engineering at research@engr.psu.edu.

IPAC is the Penn State College of Engineering’s Industrial and Professional Advisory Council, a select group of industry, government, academic, and professional representatives that advises the College on academic issues and current trends and future directions in engineering.
It acts as a link between the College and its industrial and professional partners, providing direct communication between the College and the engineering profession.
Through IPAC forums, ideas are exchanged and recommendations are made that the College uses to improve educational and research programs and address global engineering grand challenges.

For industry partners, IPAC is one of the partnership pathways listed by Penn State Engineering alongside research areas, employer relations, internships/co-ops, sponsored educational opportunities, and giving opportunities.
More information is available from the College of Engineering Alumni Relations Office at alumni@engr.psu.edu.
The College of Engineering operates centers and labs serving a variety of engineering disciplines through research, education, industry collaboration, and outreach.

Specific facilities include the Aramco High Bay Structural Testing Laboratory, which provides world-class capabilities for testing structures ranging from civil infrastructure to aerospace components at scales from benchtop models to full-size systems.
The Battery and Energy Storage Technology (BEST) Center, formed in 2011, brings together campus-wide expertise in energy storage spanning from materials to cells to systems.
The Applied Research Laboratory serves as a University Center of Excellence in naval science, systems engineering and technologies with preeminence in undersea missions.
The College also partners with interdisciplinary units including the Huck Institutes for life sciences research and the Institute for Computational and Data Sciences for advanced computing methods.

The College of Engineering partners with several interdisciplinary research units, including the Applied Research Laboratory, the Battery and Energy Storage Technology (BEST) Center, the Huck Institutes, and the Institute for Computational and Data Sciences.
The Applied Research Laboratory is a University Center of Excellence in naval science, systems engineering and technologies, with preeminence in undersea missions and related areas.
The BEST Center brings together campus-wide expertise in energy storage, fosters collaboration, and provides a focal point for research and education activities.
The Huck Institutes are dedicated to strengthening research in the life sciences, preparing students for successful careers, and encouraging new perspectives across disciplinary boundaries.

The Institute for Computational and Data Sciences supports Penn State researchers using advanced and high-performance computing methods by offering a robust cyberinfrastructure and consulting services.

The Department of Mechanical Engineering focuses on Bioinspired and Multifunctional Materials, Systems, & Structures; Biomechanics & Biodevices; Complex Flows; Engineering Education; Advanced Energy Systems; Product Design & Manufacturing; Systems, Controls, & Robotics; and Turbomachinery & Propulsion.
The department maintains numerous state-of-the-art research facilities and provides access to the Materials Research Institute to support these areas.
Faculty members also serve as directors of University-wide research centers, drawing upon the interdisciplinary strengths of Penn State.
Research is heavily supported through direct funding or collaboration with industry partners such as Lockheed Martin, Pratt & Whitney, and Solar Turbines.
You can submit your capstone project through the Learning Factory’s “Sponsor a Project” page, which notes that projects often provide direct and immediate benefits to sponsors.
Senior-year capstone design projects let companies build relationships with students and get new ideas for real design problems.
For more information about sponsoring, visit the Learning Factory website or contact Matthew Parkinson, director of The Learning Factory, at mbp11@psu.edu or 814-863-9079.
You can also contact atsbilen@psu.edu or 814-863-1526 for industry-sponsored educational opportunities.
If you want IP ownership, sponsors may request it for an additional donation of $500 per project team.
Sponsors make a donation of $4,000 to the College of Engineering to support project expenses.
Of that $4,000 donation, up to $1,250 is made available to the team for supplies and travel necessary to complete the project.
Another $1,250 covers Learning Factory expenses, with the remainder covering instructional and facilities costs on the academic department level.
Sponsors may request ownership rights of all intellectual property developed by students for an additional donation of $500 per project team.
Industry sponsors may also require each team member to sign a non-disclosure agreement for an additional donation of $500 per project team.

According to Penn State policy, undergraduate students own any intellectual property (IP) that they may develop as part of a course project.
However, students can sign over their intellectual property rights to a sponsor if requested.

Sponsors may request ownership rights of all intellectual property developed by the students during the course of the project for an additional donation of $500 per project team to help support administration expenses.
Projects in this category require students to assign their intellectual property rights to the sponsor.

Sponsors may require each team member to sign a non-disclosure agreement (Confidential Information Disclosure Agreement) for an additional donation of $500 per project team to protect company-provided information.

Sponsors may also request ownership rights of all intellectual property developed by students during the project for an additional donation of $500 per project team, which requires students to assign their IP rights to the sponsor.
The IP agreement must be requested upon project submission.
To process a Non-Disclosure Agreement, the Office of Sponsored Programs requires that the sponsor be a business entity with an Employer ID Number (EIN) or Federal Tax ID.
Sponsors who have not yet filed a patent are advised to select the confidentiality agreement option to avoid public disclosure of their invention.

Your company can engage with engineering student organizations through the Engineering Student Organizations database, which allows employers to connect with student organizations in the College of Engineering for recruiting or sponsorship purposes.
The database provides search tools to explore areas of interest, view organization support materials, and contact organizations directly.

Examples of student organizations include the Concrete Canoe Team, Developers, Earthquake Engineering Research Institute, EHouse, Energy and Mineral Engineering Graduate Student Council, Engineering - Consulting Collaborative, Engineering Graduate Student Council, Engineering Leadership Society, and Engineering Service Building Student Governing.
Many engineering student organizations have corporate sponsorship and invite industry contacts to give professional development presentations or company information sessions at general meetings.
You can search the Engineering Student Organizations database to find specific organizations that align with your company's interests.

Employers can connect with student organizations in the College of Engineering for recruiting or sponsorship purposes through the Engineering Student Organizations database, which allows them to explore areas of interest, view organization support materials, and contact organizations directly.

Additionally, companies can assist student organizations or competition teams through sponsorship programs, and for more information on the best opportunities, they can contact the College of Engineering Development Office at giving@engr.psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
Yes, Penn State College of Engineering hosts numerous student chapters of professional engineering societies.

The Student Organizations page lists chapters including the American Society of Mechanical Engineers, American Institute of Chemical Engineers, American Society of Civil Engineers, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronauts, American Nuclear Society, and American Society of Agricultural and Biological Engineers.

Additional professional societies with student chapters include the American Concrete Institute Student Chapter, Biomedical Engineering Society Student Chapter, and American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers.
The Department of Mechanical Engineering also specifically lists the American Society of Mechanical Engineers among its student organizations.
To learn more or join these organizations, visitors can contact them via their websites found on the Student Organizations page.
Yes, the Penn State College of Engineering maintains a list of engineering-themed student organizations on its "Student Organizations" page.
To learn more or join an organization, interested parties are instructed to contact them via their website, which can be found through a link on that page.
The list includes numerous groups such as the 3-D Printing Club, American Society of Mechanical Engineers, and Association for Computing Machinery.
Additionally, the Department of Mechanical Engineering website lists several student organizations, including the Society of Women Engineers and PSU Robotics Club.
Engineering Career Envoys are engineering students who have completed at least one co-op or internship experience and help promote programs supported by the office and the College of Engineering.
They are available during business hours on a walk-in basis in 117 Hammond Building and 109 ECoRE (limited hours).
You can view their current schedule online, and clicking on an Envoy's name in the calendar shows their specific location.
For questions outside of office hours, you can contact the Envoys by email.
Students in any major can talk to any of the Envoys.

The College of Engineering sponsors multiple career fairs each fall and spring, including the Fall Career Days, Engineering Career Week, and major-specific fairs like the Industrial Engineering Career Fair and Mechanical Engineering Career Fair.

Specific dates for upcoming events are listed on the Career Resources & Employer Relations Events page, which includes details like the October 22 Discover: Career Drop-In and October 28 Lockheed Martin Virtual Session.

For companies interested in hosting a custom recruiting event, the office can promote the event if you provide details such as the proposed date, time, desired degree levels and majors, and registration instructions.

Employers can participate in university-wide events like career fairs and résumé reviews, college or departmental events such as career fairs, résumé reviews, and networking receptions, and custom events tailored to their company.
The College of Engineering also offers engagement and sponsorship opportunities, including Recruiting Day, a single-employer event similar to a career fair.
Additionally, the Annual Engineering Career Event Calendar lists fall and spring semester events, such as Fall Career Days, Inspire Engineering Reception, and Engineering Impact Recruiting Event.
Employers can explore options to participate in these events through the College of Engineering's career resources.
Yes, Penn State Engineering maintains an **Annual Engineering Career Event Calendar** that lists recurring on-campus and virtual career events offered each year in the fall and/or spring semesters.
The calendar includes events such as Fall Career Days, the Engineering Impact Recruiting Event, the School of EECS Day, and various major-specific career fairs and networking receptions.
You can access this calendar through the Career Resources & Employer Relations website at career.engr.psu.edu/calendar.aspx.
Yes, Penn State Engineering offers information sessions as a type of career event where recruiters from companies or organizations can present to engineering students.
These sessions typically cover employer history, products or services, and current job opportunities, with opportunities for students to chat with recruiters afterward.

The College of Engineering's Career Resources & Employer Relations office hosts various employer events, including information sessions like the Cvent Information Session and Lockheed Martin Virtual Session.

For employers interested in hosting such events, the Recruiting Partners Program offers facilitated access to student organizations and opportunities to provide professional development presentations.
You can find more details about upcoming events and scheduling on the Career Resources & Employer Relations Events page.

However, the College of Engineering sponsors annual fall events including the Engineering Impact Recruiting Event, School of EECS Day, and various departmental career fairs, and spring events including Engineering Career Week and industryXchange.
Employers can also arrange custom recruiting events or participate in the Recruiting Partners Program for priority access to interview space and event scheduling.
Specific upcoming employer information sessions and recruiting days are listed on the Events page, such as the Amphenol Corporation Information Session and Recruiting Day.
For the most current schedule, employers should check the Annual Engineering Career Event Calendar or the Upcoming Events page.

You can make a gift to the Penn State College of Engineering through several sponsorship opportunities, including creating a fellowship, professorship, or scholarship, giving an in-kind gift, naming a facility, or supporting student organizations and programs.
For more information on the best opportunity for your company, contact the College of Engineering Development Office at giving@engr.psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
Additionally, you can support specific projects through the Penn State Learning Factory by making a $4,000 donation to the College of Engineering, which helps cover project expenses.
The College of Engineering is focused on expanding research and educational programs, and your gift can contribute to these initiatives.
For donation inquiries, contact the College of Engineering Development Office at giving@engr.psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
You can also reach out to specific staff members in the Development and Alumni Relations Directory, such as Susan Bohna, Senior Director of Major Gifts, at seb40@psu.edu or 814-865-2855.
Additionally, Bob Darrah, Senior Director of Development, can be contacted at rjd18@psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
For more information on sponsorship opportunities, visit the Penn State Engineering Sponsorship Opportunities page.
Giving to the Penn State College of Engineering supports the expansion of pioneering educational programs and broadens educational opportunities for students.
It also intensifies individual mentoring and guidance, helping students succeed.
Additionally, giving contributes to the college’s mission of preparing students for impactful careers as engineers, managers, researchers, and educators.

Corporate partners can create fellowships, professorships, or scholarships; give in-kind gifts benefiting research and education programs; name facilities, buildings, or labs; assist student organizations or competition teams; and sponsor student programs such as the Women in Engineering Program or the Multicultural Engineering Program.
The College of Engineering also offers a Recruiting Partners Program for $10,000 per fiscal year that provides strategic recruiting support and stronger access to target students.
For more information on sponsorship opportunities, contact the College of Engineering Development Office at giving@engr.psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
Alumni can get involved by being a mentor, speaking to students, creating scholarships, and hosting alumni events in their area.
They can also participate through the Penn State Engineering Alumni Society and Alumni Groups, or update their information to stay connected.
For career-related engagement, alumni are welcome to attend in-person and virtual career events to connect with employers.
Additionally, alumni can access career resources including Penn State Alumni Career Services, LionLink, and Nittany Lion Careers.

Yes, the College of Engineering offers continuing education for working engineers and professionals through short courses that provide a quick, convenient way to enhance and extend skills through high quality instruction and content.
These options are designed for employees to continue their engineering education, sometimes without leaving the office.

For students who cannot attend classes at a Penn State campus, the College also offers courses and programs that provide convenient access to quality Penn State courses and instruction at home or office.
Distance students have access to Penn State courses and resources in a sustainable, technology-based learning environment.
More information is available on the Continuing Education page at https://www.engr.psu.edu/partnership-opportunities/continuing-ed.aspx.

Penn State Engineering offers industry-sponsored educational opportunities including capstone design projects through The Learning Factory, where companies can sponsor sophisticated engineering design challenges and build relationships with students.
For more information about sponsoring a capstone design project, contact Matthew Parkinson, director of The Learning Factory, at mbp11@psu.edu or 814-863-9079.

The College of Engineering also provides additional sponsorship opportunities such as creating fellowships, professorships, or scholarships, giving in-kind gifts, naming facilities, and assisting student organizations or competition teams.
Companies can also sponsor student programs like the Women in Engineering Program or the Multicultural Engineering Program.
For more information on these opportunities, contact the College of Engineering Development Office at giving@engr.psu.edu or 814-865-0173.
The College provides short courses specifically designed for working engineers and professionals to enhance their skills through high-quality instruction, sometimes without leaving the office.
Additionally, Penn State offers distance learning courses and programs that provide convenient access to quality instruction at your home or office for those who cannot attend campus classes.
For more information, you can visit the Continuing Education page at https://www.engr.psu.edu/partnership-opportunities/continuing-ed.aspx.
